title: Protocol for Isolating and Culturing Neonatal Murine Cardiomyocytes
author: Bongiovanni, Miano, et al.
materials: DMEM F12 with stable glutamine and 15 mM HEPES

ADS buffer is a saline solution used for washing extracted hearts and for subsequent enzymatic digestion.1.Dissolve the following compounds in distilled H2O:a.3.095 g of NaCl (106 mM, Sigma 7647-14-5).b.2.385 g of HEPES (20 mM, Sigma 7365-45-9).c.0.0568 g of Na2HPO4 (0.8 mM, Sigma).d.0.197 g of KCl (5.3 mM, Sigma 7447-40-7).e.0.049 g of MgSO4×7H2O (0.4 mM, Sigma 7487-88-9).f.0.456 g of Glucose (5 mM, Sigma 50-99-7).2.Adjust the pH to 7.4 with NaOH and add distilled H2O to reach the desired volume.3.Filter the solution using a 0.22 μm filter in a biosafety cabinet and store at 4°C.CRITICAL: The ADS buffer must be used cold and can be stored for up to 2 weeks.

Cardiomyocytes and other cardiac cells are isolated from whole cardiac tissue by mechanical and enzymatic digestion. The enzyme solution used in this protocol contains Collagenase A (0.45 mg/mL) to degrade the extracellular matrix, and Pancreatin (1 mg/mL), a mixture of amylase, trypsin and lipase enzymes that facilitate protein hydrolysis.4.Transfer 22.5 mg Collagenase A (Roche 103586) and 50 mg Pancreatin (Sigma P-1750) to a 50 mL tube kept in ice.5.Add 50 mL of cold ADS buffer and vortex the mixture vigorously until the components are well mixed, though it may not become completely clear.6.Filter the solution through a 0.22-μm syringe filter in a biosafety cabinet and keep the solution on ice.CRITICAL: Prepare a fresh solution for each isolation. 50 mL of enzymes are sufficient for digesting up to 8–10 hearts.

A 0.1% gelatin solution is used as a coating treatment for polystyrene cell culture plates to facilitate murine cardiomyocyte adhesion. The plates should be pre-treated with the gelatin solution for at least 1 h in a 37°C incubator before seeding the cardiomyocytes.9.Prepare a solution in a glass bottle by dissolving 1 mg of gelatin (Sigma G9391) per mL of distilled water. For example, add 500 mg of gelatin to 500 mL of distilled water in a 500 mL glass bottle. Shake gently to mix.10.Dissolve and sterilize the solution by autoclaving.11.Allow the solution to cool to room temperature, then store it at 4°C.CRITICAL: The gelatin solution takes a considerable amount of time to cool. Therefore, it is recommended to prepare the solution at least one day before use. Store the solution for a maximum of one month.

steps.title: Prepare ADS buffer
steps.instruction: Dissolve 3.095 g NaCl, 2.385 g HEPES, 0.0568 g Na₂HPO₄, 0.197 g KCl, 0.049 g MgSO₄·7H₂O and 0.456 g glucose in distilled water; adjust pH to 7.4 with NaOH, bring to final volume, filter through a 0.22 µm filter, store at 4 °C and keep cold. Preparation takes ≈2 h; buffer can be stored up to 2 weeks.

steps.title: Make enzyme digestion solution
steps.instruction: In an ice‑cold 50 mL tube combine 22.5 mg Collagenase A (0.45 mg/mL) and 50 mg Pancreatin (1 mg/mL) with 50 mL cold ADS buffer, vortex vigorously, filter through a 0.22 µm syringe filter, keep on ice. Prepare fresh for each isolation; 50 mL is sufficient for 8–10 hearts. Preparation takes ≈30 min.

steps.title: Prepare cardiac adhesion medium
steps.instruction: In a biosafety cabinet mix 81 % DMEM‑F12 (with stable Glutamine and 15 mM HEPES), 10 % fetal bovine serum, 5 % horse serum, 1 % penicillin/streptomycin (100 X), 1 % glutamine (200 mM), 1 % non‑essential amino‑acid solution (100 X) and 1 % sodium pyruvate (100 mM); filter through a 0.22 µm filter and pre‑warm at 37 °C before use. Preparation takes ≈15 min.

steps.title: Prepare 0.1 % gelatin solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 1 mg gelatin per mL distilled water (e.g., 500 mg in 500 mL) in a glass bottle, shake gently, autoclave to sterilize, allow to cool to room temperature, then store at 4 °C (maximum 1 month). Prepare at least one day before coating; the preparation requires ≈1 day (including cooling).

steps.title: Coat plates with gelatin
steps.instruction: Add enough 0.1 % gelatin solution to completely cover each polystyrene culture plate, incubate 1 h at 37 °C, then aspirate excess solution and keep plates at 4 °C until cell seeding.

steps.title: Extract and wash neonatal hearts
steps.instruction: Sacrifice neonatal (post‑natal day 0 or 1) mice by decapitation, aseptically remove the hearts, place them in cold ADS buffer (pH 7.4) in a Petri dish, cut at the ventricular level, gently press with curved‑pointed tweezers to remove excess blood, and sterilize scissors/tweezers with 70 % ethanol then dry thoroughly. Perform quickly under a laminar flow hood.

steps.title: First washing digestion (10 min)
steps.instruction: Transfer the hearts to the inner edge of a 50 mL self‑standing conical tube containing a cylindrical magnetic bar, add 8 mL pre‑warmed enzyme solution, place the tube on a magnetic stirrer inside a 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ incubator, stir slowly for 10 min, then aspirate 7 mL supernatant with a serological pipette set to minimum speed, leaving 1 mL enzyme solution to keep the tissue suspended.

steps.title: Four enzymatic digestions (20 min each)
steps.instruction:
Repeat the following cycle four times (total ≈3 h):
1. Add 7 mL pre‑warmed enzyme solution to the tube (use 4 mL if processing only 3–5 hearts).
2. Stir gently at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ for 20 min.
3. Transfer the supernatant to a 15 mL tube containing 1 mL horse serum to inactivate enzymes.
4. Centrifuge at 400 g (brake 6) for 5 min.
5. Discard supernatant and gently resuspend the pellet in 2 mL adhesion medium.
6. Return the tube to the incubator with the cap slightly loosened for gas exchange.
During all transfers use the minimum aspiration speed and leave 1 mL enzyme solution to avoid aspirating tissue. The procedure is less efficient with fewer than three hearts.

steps.title: Pool and resuspend final cell pellet
steps.instruction: Collect the cell suspensions from the fourth digestion into a single 15 mL tube, centrifuge at 400 g (brake 6) for 5 min, discard supernatant, and gently resuspend the pellet in 4 mL adhesion medium (or 2 mL if fewer than five hearts). Avoid vigorous or prolonged resuspension to preserve cell integrity.

steps.title: Count cells and seed onto plates
steps.instruction: Determine cell concentration and seed onto gelatin‑coated plates using adhesion medium: 35 000 cells per well in 96‑well plates for immunofluorescence, or 400 000–500 000 cells per well in 12‑well plates for protein or gene‑expression analyses.

steps.title: Optional cardiomyocyte enrichment
steps.instruction: If higher cardiomyocyte purity is required, perform magnetic‑activated cell sorting with the MACS Neonatal Isolation System (Miltenyi Biotec #130‑100‑825) following the manufacturer’s protocol, or employ a pre‑plating step to allow non‑cardiomyocytes to adhere before collecting the enriched cardiomyocyte‑rich supernatant.
